Well said, the premise of this statement is false. In non-formal logic this fallacy is called Reductico Ad Absurdum. It's more a rationalization for continuing to overeat than 'memories.'

Reductico Ad Absurdum is not a fallacy. The fallacy here is the black and white fallacy which is to make the claim that you can only do 1 of 2 choices and one will always be to the detriment of the other. You can enjoy family and the holidays, eat generously, and maintain a healthy weight easily.

Reductico ad absurdum is a technique to expose a poorly thought through idea by taking it to its logical conclusion and demonstrating the absurd consequences of that idea. The classic "If all your friends jumped off a bridge, would you do so too?" is a reductico ad absurdum.

I think you might be thinking of the sunken cost fallacy, which is to claim that you're already fat so you might as well get even fatter over Christmas; or the strawman fallacy, which is to claim that people who advocate not stuffing yourself to bursting over Christmas are advocating for starving yourself.

A bad example of reductio ad absurdum is when people start to say, "You can't buy someone a hat to make them feel better because then you would have to buy everyone a hat and then shoes and pants." They are not extending the idea to its logical conclusion because the original claim was just buying 1 hat for 1 person. Whereas claiming that "If you must buy a hat just because it's on sale, then you must buy anything just because it's on sale" extends the logic of "I must because X." The two concepts are similar, but there is a subtle distinction.
